name: capsule-render
one_liner: The category incumbent: URL-parameterized SVG header/footer generator for GitHub READMEs, 15 shape/animation effect types with arbitrary colors, gradients and text.
price: Free (MIT). GitHub Sponsors enabled for kyechan99 — custom amount only, no preset tiers.
adoption: 1,790 stars, 731 forks, 11 open issues (fetched 2026-08-04 via GitHub REST API). Created 2020-07-17. GitHub Sponsors: exactly 1 sponsor.
last_activity: 2026-07-25 (pushed_at) — ACTIVELY MAINTAINED, 3 issues closed in June 2026
strengths: 298x the stars of the product (1,790 vs 6) — it IS the default answer devs already reach for
731 forks means a large self-hosted long tail immune to the maintainer's own infra failing
Actively maintained in 2026 — issues closed 2026-06-08 and 2026-06-12, pushed 2026-07-25
README translated into 11 languages (de/es/fr/jp/kr/ml/pt-br/ru/zh-cn/zh-hk/zh-tw) — real international distribution
Its 15 types are COMPOSABLE primitives (any color/gradient/text/animation), so its effective output space is unbounded — arguably larger expressive range than 359 fixed presets
Has a test suite (jest, snapshot tests), commitlint, husky — mature engineering hygiene
Honest about its own limits: README tells users to fork and self-host for production
positioning_vs_you: As a user: with capsule-render you pick a shape and hand-tune colors, so you get something nobody else has but you have to make design decisions. With the product you scroll a gallery and pick a finished look. The product wins on 'I want it to look good and I don't want to think'; capsule-render wins on 'I want MY colors' and on the social proof of being the tool everyone already uses.

kills_your_moat.why: On a literal count of named presets, 359 > 15, so 'largest animated README banner collection' survives — but only under a narrow reading. capsule-render's 15 types are parameterized primitives, not presets: any color/gradient/text combination is reachable, so its reachable output space is effectively infinite. The claim is true as stated and misleading as heard. A skeptic who reads 'largest collection' as 'most things you can make' will find the claim false.

name: readme-typing-svg
one_liner: Animated typing-effect SVG text for READMEs, embedded as a single URL — the most-adopted animated-SVG README tool found.
price: Free (MIT). GitHub Sponsors tiers $1/$3/$5/$10/$20/$25/$35/$100 per month, plus Ko-fi (jlawrence).
adoption: 9,169 stars, 1,594 forks, 68 open issues (fetched 2026-08-04 via GitHub REST API). Created 2021-04-20. GitHub Sponsors: 4 current sponsors against a stated goal of 10.
strengths: 1,528x the stars of the product (9,169 vs 6) — the single most-adopted animated README SVG tool in the sweep
1,594 forks = enormous self-hosted tail
Has a real support community (Discord server) — no other player in this category does
Most complete monetization attempt in the category (8 sponsor tiers + Ko-fi + YouTube), so it is the best available evidence on what this category can earn
Deploy-to-Heroku button plus demolab.com demo — deliberate multi-host strategy reduces single-point-of-failure risk
positioning_vs_you: Not a substitute in a strict sense — it animates TEXT typing, the product animates a gradient BACKGROUND. But as a user experiences it, both fill the same slot: the animated strip at the top of my README. Most devs pick one, not both. It is a competitor for the slot, not for the feature.

kills_your_moat.why: Different effect class (typing text vs gradient background) and it does not ship a large preset library, so it does not refute a 'largest collection' claim. It does, however, refute any claim that this is an underserved niche — 9,169 stars says the niche is well served and already has a winner.

Hosted on GitHub Pages (github.io), which is free and effectively never goes down — no per-request cost at all

name: readme-aura (collectioneur)
one_liner: Render React/JSX components as animated SVGs directly inside GitHub READMEs — a generalization that subsumes banner generation.
adoption: 138 stars, 9 forks (fetched 2026-08-04 via GitHub REST API).
strengths: 23x the product's stars and rising fast on a repo that is being pushed to daily

STRATEGICALLY THE MOST DANGEROUS ENTRY IN THE SWEEP: if you can render arbitrary JSX to animated SVG, a banner is just one component — a 359-template library becomes an npm package someone publishes on top of it
npm distribution rather than a hosted URL, so it has no hosting cost and no outage surface
Generalizes the category instead of competing inside it
positioning_vs_you: As a user: the product gives you a finished banner from a menu; readme-aura gives you the ability to build any animated README graphic you can code, banner included. It converts 'pick from my gallery' into 'write your own', which is how preset libraries historically get commoditized.

kills_your_moat.why: Not on count — it ships no competing preset library. But it dissolves the terms of the claim: if arbitrary JSX renders to animated README SVG, 'largest collection of templates' stops being a moat because templates become trivially user-authorable and forkable. A moat measured in preset count does not survive a general-purpose renderer gaining traction.

name: GitHub / Camo image proxy (PLATFORM)
one_liner: GitHub proxies every README image through its Camo image proxy, which sits between the product's server and every reader.
adoption: Universal — every image in every GitHub README passes through it.
strengths: GitHub controls content-type support, caching and sanitization for every README image, unilaterally and without notice

Camo caching is governed by Cache-Control headers — GitHub docs explicitly tell publishers to return 'no-cache' if images must update, meaning stale/frozen renders are a known, documented failure mode for dynamic image services
Camo maintains an allowlist of supported content types; GitHub docs acknowledge unsupported content types are simply not proxied
positioning_vs_you: As a user, nothing about the product is under its own control at the moment of viewing: the banner your reader sees is fetched, cached and sanitized by GitHub. A single GitHub policy change on SVG handling or caching would alter or break every banner in every README simultaneously, with no recourse.

kills_your_moat.why: Does not refute the template-count claim, but it caps the value of the entire category: the product owns neither distribution nor rendering. This is a concentration risk, not a competitor.

sources.what_it_supports: 'To host your images, GitHub uses the open-source project Camo.' Cache-Control/no-cache guidance for images that must update; acknowledgement that unsupported content types are not proxied

name: Self-hosting / forking (THE REAL SUBSTITUTE)
one_liner: Fork any of these MIT tools and deploy to your own free Vercel/GitHub Pages account — the incumbent literally instructs users to do this.
price: $0 — Vercel and GitHub Pages free tiers cover README-banner traffic.
adoption: capsule-render 731 forks + readme-typing-svg 1,594 forks + github-readme-stats 36,149 forks = 38,474 forks of directly comparable tools (fetched 2026-08-04).
strengths: Free forever, no rate limits, no dependency on any maintainer
MIT licensing means the product's own 359 templates can be forked wholesale by anyone, including a competitor — the library is copyable, so it is not a defensible asset
capsule-render's README actively RECOMMENDS this path for production use, so the incumbent is training users away from hosted dependence
positioning_vs_you: As a user: ten minutes of setup buys permanent independence. Anyone burned once by a broken README image takes this path and never returns to a hosted generator.

kills_your_moat.why: The template library is MIT-licensed content, not a service advantage. Anyone can fork all 359 templates and self-host them, so 'largest collection' is a lead measured in someone else's copy time, not a moat. Nothing prevents a competitor from ingesting the whole library legally.

No paid tier, no commercial license, no hosted-plan upsell was found on any of them. The category's revenue ceiling, as evidenced, is a few dollars per month at 10,000-star scale.
